comment: Took her for Micro Theory (ECON 271). Found class to be interesting and even though it is a hard class, with practice and good note taking it wasn't that bad. Having experience in math ahead of time for Micro Theory is very beneficial but all material was learned during classtime.

The exam questions do not relate to what was taught in class. She says it's because she doesn't want us to just memorize but she doesn't teach what is on the exams. We would do problems in class that weren't possible. Took her for Micro-Theory, she was the only professor. Would try and get a different professor if possible.

Inaccurate/incomplete syllabus. Typos on every homework/study guide and doesn't fix. Unclear lectures, examples that don't make sense. Graded problem sets on stuff that is not covered in class or in the textbook. No one knows what is going on. You have to teach yourself this class. Do. Not. Take.
Be prepared to teach your self everything. Very tough grader. Unclear expectations. Lectures often unrelated to homework and tests. Often expected to know how to do problems not taught in class.

She is a super smart and supportive person. Although most students would feel stressed at first, you will finally realize another economic world because of her! She taught us not only the fundamental economic theories but also the real economic world (the difference between reality and economic models) and popular behavioral economics, etc.

Dr. Linask is a very nice woman. She is very understanding and cares about her students. However, her tests and problem sets are too hard. She prides herself in assigning lots of work and allowing retakes on quizzes and problem sets so it is hard to fail. This is true, you won't fail but it feels impossible to do well since everything is so hard.

While Dr. Linask is a good person, her teaching, on the other hand, is okay. Her class is very lecture heavy and she can be a little vague. There is A LOT of homework, and she has high expectations for her Econ101 (a bit too high for people starting, but I digress.) Getting to her outside of class can be a hassle too, but is attainable.

I really love Dr. Linask as a person and I often enjoy going to class. Her homework though, and exams are very difficult. She expects a lot out of her students which isn't bad, but she does not provide adequate help out of class to make this happen. I wouldn't recommend taking her for ECON101 because I have heard she is the most difficult one...
Lectures are unclear and very unhelpful in office hours

I really enjoyed my class with Dr Linask because she was a really engaging professor. She was super approachable and I wasn't scared to ask her any questions. The worst part of the course was having to read a book but it was all put into context. I found her enthusiasm for econ really inspiring and would love to have taken more classes from her.

This professor cannot teach at all. She just goes over examples during class that are not helpful and she doesn't teach the concepts. She just makes you learn everything outside of class which means there's tons of work. Maybe other students feel differently but I would not recommend this class.

Very nice professor who is very interested in economics. She is good at explaining. You'll understand the concepts, but the tests are too long. There isn't enough time to finish them. The textbook is not that helpful. The online quizzes are harder than you'd expect and take like an hour each. Problem sets are a good studying mechanism.

Worst professor for mico econ. Her tests and problem sets do not make any sense. She gave out two midterms that were so long that only about 3-4 people finished on time. She words her tests and problem sets in a weird way and tends to take off points for any small mistake. She does understand her material and lectures well, just grades tough
worst lecture i took in bschool. 40 min nothing and 30 min lecture. useless discussions that take way much time than necessary. Learned nothing, basically nothing.

If you are a woman interested in business, take Dr. Linask!! She is so freaking awesome. Micro is going to be hard with whoever you take, but Dr. Linask teaches like a helpful high school teacher which is perfect for freshman. There is a lot of opportunities to raise your grade, and her homework is long but is the exact preparation for her exams.

Dr. Linask's microeconomics class was HARD. That being said, she is one of the greatest professors. She really makes you work for the grade. There are online quizzes which seem to be extra, but they are open note and open person (so not too bad). Her tests, on the other hand, are killer and you really need to know your stuff.

Very good professor! Dr. Linask is really passionate, giving clear lectures with vivd examples. Getting an A definitely requires a decent amount of efforts put into class materials and assorted kinds of assignments (nothing extremely hard). But she really teaches you how to apply basic micro to the real world, making it tangible. Liked her a lot!

Really interesting and engaging professor. I took the class just because I was interested in econ even though I am not majoring in business. Her class is challenging and I would suggest really making sure to pick up points on quizzes and problem sets because you most likely will loose some on the tests.

She is a great teacher. She cares more about the individual and learning than the grade. If you plan ahead, she will gladly grant extensions. She is always willing to help and tutors are extremely accessible. She wants every student to succeed and will try her best to aid in this. She is not as tough of a grader as people make her out to be.

This professor makes econ really interesting and engaging. She applies the concepts that we learn to the real world with experiments and articles. She really values participation in class and has a great sense of humor.

Dr Linask is very smart as evidenced by her degree from Harvard however she is a horrible professor who assigns triple the amount of work then other intro to Econ profs. Prepare to work twice as hard and get a lower grade than your peers tAking intro to micro. DO NOT TAKE her class unless you absolutely have to. Get out now !!

She was nice and the class was interesting overall, but she was very difficult.  I thought I would do much better in the class than I did.  She is a very tough grader and will mark off a lot of points for mistakes.  She is nice though to students.

I was very interested in economics before i signed up for her class. She was very easy to understand and her class was straightforward. Her exams were challenging, but there were other ways to bring up your grade. She was also very helpful with any questions or concerns I had relating to the class.

Dr. Linask is very nice, and teaches in a friendly manner. Depending on how quick you are to pick concepts up, it is  easy to fall behind in this class. Lots of notes, and the tests are very difficult. However, there are a ton of ways to make up points due to her unique grading system. If you nail the homework and online quizzes, you're golden.

She really cares about her students doing well, and is always willing to meet with anyone to help them do better.  She assigns reading but then goes over the same material in class, which is very helpful.  It is easy to get at least a B if you are willing to work for it.  I completely recommend her!

Not as bad as everyone else is saying.  I had never taken an economics class prior to this one and I received an A with minimal effort and work.  She improved greatly from the beginning of the semester, which is expected of a new teacher.  Do the problem sets with a partner and you should be alright.

DO NOT TAKE! Im good at Econ and it was still impossible to get a good grade int his class. Everyone fails the problem sets which are 1/3 of your grade. If you take, make sure to go to her to look over problem sets. But curves for tests are very good

She grades too harshly. You will only get an A in her class if and only if you go to all her office hours for clarifications because it is what she likes. She is simply the worst teacher I've ever had throughout my entire life at school so so far. I strongly recommend not taking her class because it is not worthy and you won't learn anything.

She is a tough professor for those who have never taken any kind of economics before. She assigns readings but never goes over them in class. She assumes that we know everything. From the beginning to the end of class, it's pretty much all graphing. I tried to schedule several appointments with her outside her office hours, but never happened.

Nobody pays attention to her because she doesn't make much sense and we often correct her (at the beginning, now we're just bored) so now she corrects herself which happens too much. Don't take her if you want a strong understanding of microeconomics. If you just want an easy B or work for the A then she's not a horrible choice.

She doesn't teach in a way that is understandable to students. The majority of the time the students have no idea what she's talking about. If you've taken econ before you'll be fine. If you haven't, she doesn't teach well enough for you to get a good grade. She grades really harshly! Especially the problem sets, which take hours to finish

She is new to this school, but she is still a very weird teacher. No one has any idea what is going in class. The upside is that she is sooooo hot. It's actually incredible. A perfect 10. At least she's somethin to look at cause she's not much to learn at.
